documents.title: Select an existing activity and Quick actions
documents.content: The toolbar above the activity form provides New activity, Select an existing activity, and Quick actions. New activity resets the form. Select an existing activity searches open activities by subject, notes, linked client, or linked project; enable Show completed activities to include completed records. Quick actions mirrors the signed-in user's Favorite Actions from My Shortcuts in the same order, and Manage favorites opens the existing customization screen. To finish an activity, set its Status to Done and Save. Timer controls and Log actual time are in the Time Sessions card, the meeting agenda is under More tools beside Notes, and Delete Activity is at the bottom of the form. Switching records or following an internal Quick action asks before discarding unsaved edits.

documents.title: Subject, Notes and the activity form fields
documents.content: Open Activity Manager at /event-manager. There is no Action, Project, or Note chooser: every activity is filled in the same way. Enter the required Subject, then set When, and optionally Client, Project, Assign to, and Notes. Client, Project, and Assign to are optional searchable dropdowns. Behind the scenes a new activity is stored as a task; an older appointment, project, or note record keeps its stored type when opened and saved. To link an activity to a project, use the Project dropdown.

documents.title: How Next free slot chooses a time
documents.content: For a new activity opened directly in Activity Manager, the When band defaults to Next free slot. Ogeemo searches the selected assignee's scheduled, unfinished, timed events for the first 30-minute gap inside 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. It searches today from the next five-minute boundary, then subsequent weekdays. Today is still allowed on a weekend. Completed, all-day, unscheduled, and untimed items do not block a slot. The suggestion follows an assignee change until the user edits the date or time. If no suitable time exists within 14 days, no slot is suggested.

documents.title: When choices and schedule preservation
documents.content: The When band under Subject has three choices: Next free slot, Pick a time, and No set time. Next free slot supplies a calendar-based suggestion. Pick a time keeps scheduling enabled and lets the user choose Start, End, or All-day. No set time saves the activity unscheduled. Editing a suggested date or time changes the band to Pick a time so later refreshes do not overwrite the user's choice. Opening an existing event or arriving through a calendar handoff preserves that event's own schedule instead of applying the new-activity suggestion.

documents.title: Save, Save & New, Cancel and Delete
documents.content: Save, Save & New, and Cancel are in a row at the top of Activity Manager, above the New activity, Select an existing activity, and Quick actions toolbar. Save stores the activity and returns to the previous page. Save & New stores it, refreshes the calendar used for availability, resets the form, and suggests another free slot so the just-used time is not reused. Cancel asks before discarding unsaved edits, then returns to the previous page. A Subject is required before Save or Save & New. Delete Activity is at the bottom of the form when editing an existing activity; deletion returns Activity Manager to a clean New activity state.

documents.title: Time sessions and billing
documents.content: The Time Sessions card records actual work on an activity. Start a session to run the timer; pause, resume, or log the session as needed. The Log actual time button in the same card adds a manual hours-and-minutes session ending now for a saved activity, and the Calendar's Log Actual Time link opens the same dialog for the selected activity. Actual sessions take precedence over the planned schedule span for recorded duration. Mark as billable controls whether the activity can be included on an invoice and reveals the hourly rate. Status can be To Do, In Progress, or Done. Scheduled time by itself is planning information, not automatically billable work.
